_about: Real photos for the Photo Archive gallery (tools/render_archive_gallery.py). Every file is from Wikimedia Commons, public domain or CC BY / CC BY-SA; the credit line is baked onto each slide. Captions are written from the file's own description and the stop's checked cards (tools/story-cards.json).

photos.file: File:Western entrance to inner quadrangle, Leland Stanford Junior University-LCCN2008678137.jpg
photos.headline: The Inner Quad's western gate
photos.caption: Palms and sandstone at the western entrance to the Inner Quad, within a decade of opening day.
photos.credit: Detroit Publishing Co. · Library of Congress · Public domain

photos.file: File:East side of quadrangle of Leland Stanford, Jr. University (no 51253) - Detroit Photographic Company.jpg
photos.headline: The arcades, brand new
photos.caption: The Quad's east side on a hand-colored photochrom postcard, the long arcade fresh from the quarry.
photos.credit: Detroit Photographic Co. · Beinecke Library, Yale · Public domain

photos.file: File:View of the chapel from the corridor at Stanford University (CHS-1851).jpg
photos.headline: Memorial Church through the arches
photos.caption: The church seen from the Quad's corridor, with the tall spire the 1906 earthquake would bring down.
photos.credit: California Historical Society · USC Digital Library · Public domain

photos.file: File:The massive arch at Stanford University (CHS-1850).jpg
photos.headline: The Memorial Arch
photos.caption: The grand arch at the Quad's entrance, crowned by a carved frieze of soldiers and horses.
photos.credit: California Historical Society · USC Digital Library · Public domain

photos.file: File:San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Entrance gate at Stanford University - NARA - 513318.tif
photos.headline: The arch becomes a ghost
photos.caption: The earthquake left the Memorial Arch a broken shell. It came down; only its bases still mark the spot.
photos.credit: W. E. Worden · U.S. National Archives · Public domain

photos.headline: The engineering anchor
photos.caption: Huang Center opened in 2010 at the head of the Science and Engineering Quad.
photos.credit: Photo: Frank Schulenburg · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

photos.headline: The name over the door
photos.caption: Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center, carved beside the main entrance.
photos.credit: Photo: Leijurv · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

photos.headline: Huang and the NVIDIA Auditorium
photos.caption: The Huang building (left) and the NVIDIA Auditorium wing (right), across the lawn.
photos.credit: Photo: Jim Heaphy (Cullen328) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

photos.headline: Jensen Huang, back at Stanford
photos.caption: The NVIDIA co-founder speaks at a Stanford GSB discussion on U.S. leadership in AI.
photos.credit: Photo: Anders Eidesvik · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

photos.headline: In the classroom
photos.caption: Huang (right) at a fireside chat in Stanford's CS 153 course.
photos.credit: Photo: Anders Eidesvik · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

photos.headline: Hoover, as students drew him
photos.caption: A caricature of Herbert Hoover, from Stanford's first graduating class, in the 1900 Stanford Quad yearbook.

photos.file: File:Herbert Hoover, head and shoulders portrait, as a young man, facing right LCCN2005694773.jpg
photos.headline: Herbert Hoover
photos.caption: The Stanford geology graduate around the time he ran U.S. food relief in World War I.

photos.file: File:Tower, Hoover Institute and Library, Stanford - Front.png
photos.headline: The tower on a postcard
photos.caption: Hoover Tower opened in 1941 to house his archive of war and peace.

photos.headline: The carillon bells
photos.caption: Bells of the carillon, which shares the tower's 14th floor with the observation deck.

photos.caption: Wildfire smoke turned the sky orange over Jane Stanford Way and the tower.
